title: Dates on the pages are in Japan time
text: The Terms of Use now say that the dates on Sophaxis's pages, in this feed, in the notices and in the news are dates in Japan time, and that the day a text was fetched is the day in UTC that the record of the fetch keeps. Two entries of this feed, published on 2026-11-13 in Japan time, were dated 2026-11-12, the date by the clock of the work; they are now dated 2026-11-13, and the change to the Copyright Policy took effect on publication, not earlier. The "Last updated" of the pages changed that day is now 2026-11-13. This narrows no right and adds no duty.

title: The day from which each place is not offered, in the Privacy Policy
text: The Privacy Policy said, of the Zenodo community and of the people in the other places that the Submission Policy lists, that the rule applies from 2026-11-22. The Submission Policy gives 2026-11-26 for 15 of the 43 places, as announced. The Privacy Policy now says that the rule applies from the date the Submission Policy gives for each place: 2026-11-22, or 2026-11-26 for 15 of them. Nothing that Sophaxis does changes, and no right is narrowed.

title: PDFs are no longer copied by script from Figshare or Research Square
text: Effective on publication, 2026-11-13: Sophaxis copies PDFs by script only from Zenodo and arXiv, whose own pages let a script fetch them. Until then, it also copied from Figshare and Research Square, whose terms forbid robots and scripts. The authors of a work at either can attach the deposited PDF to the submission issue instead, as for every other repository. This narrows what authors get. Going on would act against the terms of the two repositories, a legal risk, so the change takes effect on publication, as the Terms of Use allow when a legal risk requires a change sooner, and not earlier. The copies already taken from Figshare stay.

title: In a dispute, the operator aims to answer within 7 days, and a pause holds the answer
text: From 2026-11-26, the Terms of Use say that, in a dispute, the operator aims to answer within 7 days and does not leave a dispute without reply, and that during a pause described under "Continuity" the answer waits until the pause ends. Until then, the operator answers within 7 days. The words promised an answer in 7 days even while the operator cannot work on Sophaxis at all, which the Terms already allow for; this weakens a promise, so it is announced 14 days ahead. The call for advisers and the policies in brief say the same from the same day.

title: Texts by others kept for verification are not under CC BY 4.0
text: The Licence Policy and the Terms of Use now say that texts by others that the repository quotes, or keeps to verify its quotations, are not licensed under CC BY 4.0 and remain their owners'. They never were the operator's to license. From today the repository keeps whole only laws and other texts that Japan's Copyright Act, Article 13, leaves outside copyright; of every other text it keeps the address, the day, the SHA-256 of the text as fetched, and the parts it quotes or relies on. This narrows no right that anyone held.

title: Fifteen more places where Sophaxis is not offered, and what a person in New Zealand is told
text: From 2026-11-26, Sophaxis is not offered in 15 more places: Argentina, Colombia, Ghana, Korea, Mexico, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar. A survey of the laws of 195 countries was made on 2026-11-12, and the data protection laws it found were read at their sources by number. The laws of these places ask for registration, for conditions before personal data leaves the place, for the operator's postal address or telephone number before personal data is collected, or for a parent's consent that the service confirms before the data of a minor is processed; or their data protection law could not be read at its source. The Submission Policy names the law of each. This narrows who can be listed, so it is announced 14 days ahead. From today, the Privacy Policy and the submission form also say that the services outside Japan may not be required to protect personal data with safeguards comparable to those of the law where an author lives, as New Zealand's Privacy Act 2020 asks a person there to be told, and that, for a person in Switzerland, the disclosure to the United States rests on explicit consent; this narrows no right.

title: The rules on sending users' information outside are met as if they applied
text: The Privacy Policy now meets the rules of Japan's Telecommunications Business Act on sending users' information outside as if they applied to Sophaxis, and gives, for the one request that a page makes a reader's browser send (the search page's request for the list of records), what is sent, who handles it and for what purpose. The Ministry's Ordinance was fetched and read. None of this narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: The agreement on the court covers only suits based on the Terms
text: From 2026-11-26, the agreement on the court of first instance, made in a form, covers only suits based on the Terms of Use, or on the submission, listing, correction, withdrawal or removal of the person's own works under them, so that it stays within what Japan's Code of Civil Procedure allows to be agreed. For any other dispute, the court that the law sets has jurisdiction. The agreement stays non-exclusive, and talks and mediation still come first. This may narrow the disputes that can be brought to the agreed court, so it is announced 14 days ahead.

title: The mailbox and the request logs, the system of the United States, and the records of provision
text: The Privacy Policy says that the operator's mailbox at iCloud Mail is provided to users in Japan by iTunes K.K., a company in Japan, which Sophaxis treats as entrusted with it, so that it is not a provision to a third party in a foreign country and no consent is asked of the people who write; that Apple Inc. may handle the emails in the United States; and that Vercel's request logs are not personal information for Sophaxis, with the reasons. It now gives the Personal Information Protection Commission's own information on the system of the United States, what Anthropic says of its measures, and why the measures of OpenAI and xAI cannot be given. It names docs/records-of-provision.md, which gives each recipient's name and address, as part of the record of provision to third parties, kept for at least three years. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: Why the rules on sending users' information do not apply, Sophaxis as the sender of its records, and the texts fetched again
text: The Privacy Policy says why the operator considers that the rules of Japan's Telecommunications Business Act on sending users' information outside do not apply: Sophaxis charges for nothing and earns nothing, so it runs no telecommunications business. The Takedown Policy says that, for the record pages and the PDF copies, Sophaxis is itself the sender under Japan's Act on providers of specified telecommunications services, so it does not rely on that Act's limitation of liability, and the operator is liable as Japanese law provides. The texts that the policies quote were fetched again on 2026-11-12, and the Privacy and Submission Policies now quote Article 1 of Russia's Federal Law No. 152-FZ. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: A first sentence for each policy, the steps while the operator cannot work, and numbers in the Japanese translations
text: Each policy now opens with a sentence that says what it is. The Terms of Use set out, under Continuity, what happens while the operator cannot work at all: who is told, what is paused, what stays online, what still works without the operator, and who could take over. The Japanese translations write durations and dates in Arabic digits, as the English does. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: How the criteria for listing change, a feed for policy changes, and no counts of views
text: The Moderation Policy says how the criteria for listing are reviewed and changed: at least once a year and when a law or a service changes, under the same rules as every other policy, with 14 days' notice for a change that narrows what can be listed. The Terms of Use say that each change to a policy is entered in this feed, which carries nothing else. The Privacy Policy says that no page shows a count of views or downloads, and that Sophaxis keeps no such count. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty.

title: Changes announced on the top page, before this feed began
text: Changes to these policies were announced on the top page before this feed began. They take effect in steps, from 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-25, as the notice on the top page and each policy say.

title: The feed begins
text: Each of the eight policies was last changed on 2026-11-11. Earlier versions, and every change to them, are kept in the history of the public repository. From this day, each change to a policy is also entered here.
